section_1.title: The Hook: The Broken Pencil Illusion
section_1.content: Introduce the phenomenon using a visual contrast: a pencil placed in a half-filled water glass appears 'broken' at the surface. Briefly establish that light travels in straight lines in a vacuum but changes behavior when entering denser matter.
section_1.example: An animation showing a pencil entering water and the light rays 'kinking' at the air-water interface.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Speed of Light in Media
section_2.content: Define the refractive index (n) as a ratio: n = c/v. Explain that light slows down in denser media (like glass or water) compared to a vacuum. Use the analogy of a marching band moving from pavement onto thick mud.
section_2.example: A row of marchers represented by a line of light waves; as the front wheels (or marchers) hit the mud, they slow down, causing the entire line to pivot/turn.

section_3.title: Snell’s Law: The Mathematical Geometry
section_3.content: Introduce Snell’s Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use a clear graphic showing the 'Normal' line perpendicular to the surface. Focus on the relationship between the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction.
section_3.example: An interactive diagram where dragging the incident light beam dynamically updates the angles and the sine values in real-time.

section_4.title: Visualizing Direction: Toward or Away from Normal
section_4.content: Establish the rule: When moving from low-density (fast) to high-density (slow), light bends toward the normal. Moving from high to low, it bends away. Connect this to the 'marching band' analogy.
section_4.example: Split-screen animation: One side showing air-to-glass (bending inward), the other showing glass-to-air (bending outward).

section_5.title: Application: The Archer Fish
section_5.content: Apply the concept to a real-world predator: The Archer Fish. It must compensate for light refraction to accurately spit water at insects above the surface. Summarize the lesson by noting that our eyes must account for this 'virtual image' shift.
section_5.example: An animation of an Archer Fish looking up; show the 'apparent' position of the bug vs. its 'true' position, and the adjustment the fish makes to strike.
